entry.title: Route Anything: A Study of Model and Policy Routing for General-Purpose AI Systems
entry.summary:
Artificial general intelligence (AGI) requires a method that can understand, generate, reason, and act across diverse domains and modalities. Rather than relying on a single model to master every capability, a promising path toward AGI now is to orchestrate a heterogeneous ecosystem of specialized models, tools, and policies (candidates) into a unified AI system. At the heart of this vision lies a fundamental question: how can an AI system dynamically select and coordinate the most capable candidate for each task while balancing performance and computational cost?

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #agents #robotics

entry.title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
entry.summary:
Learning a universal action representation from video requires modeling dynamics that are consistent across different executions of the same action yet invariant to changes in embodiment and appearance. Existing latent action models infer actions from visual transitions, but their representations often entangle the underlying action with irrelevant visual variations, limiting transfer across embodiments. We introduce DreamX, which repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a universal latent action learner.

entry.title: Words Caught in the Heart: Simulating Person-Specific Expression for Self-Opaque Clients in Psychotherapy
entry.summary:
Psychotherapy clients may experience distress before they can coherently describe it, and their expression changes with emotion, perceived safety, and trust. Large language model-based client simulators often rely on clinically organized case descriptions, which can encourage responses explaining the client's difficulties more clearly than their current understanding warrants. We propose Pandora, a psychotherapy client simulation framework that models how psychological experience becomes situated, individual expression.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #rust

entry.title: Think Less, Locally: Local Preference Learning for Reasoning Compression
entry.summary:
Large reasoning models achieve strong performance on challenging tasks, but their long chain-of-thought often incurs substantial inference costs by continuing to deliberate after sufficient information has been obtained. Existing reasoning compression methods primarily operate on reasoning trajectories, paying less attention to the local decision of whether further reasoning is necessary given the current state. We propose LoCo, a local preference learning method for reasoning compression.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights

entry.title: YANAMI: A Large-Scale Multimodal Dataset and Benchmark for Multiturn Stateful Interaction
entry.summary:
Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) integrate visual understanding, generation, and editing within a single unified framework. However, existing unified multimodal datasets and benchmarks remain dominated by single-turn tasks. Even in recent multi-turn datasets, many turns can be solved independently without tracking information across turns.

entry.title: Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified
entry.summary:
We introduce Axion 1.0, a fully open agent foundation model that combines strong and broad agentic capabilities with a remarkably simple training recipe. Axion 1.0 is trained in only three stages: two lightweight supervised fine-tuning stages followed by reinforcement learning, without dedicated mid-training, direct preference optimization (DPO), or on-policy distillation (OPD). The first SFT stage develops strong self-contained reasoning through model-aware data construction, where we synthesize challenging problems and adversarially strengthen them based on the base model's own successful solution strategies.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #agents #reinforcement-learning

entry.title: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents
entry.summary:
Large language models are deployed as long-horizon agents that compose diverse tools across MCP services into executable workflows. Existing MCP environment-scaling methods are data-centric: they first synthesize a database and scenario, then derive tools and tasks from them. As a result, tool interfaces may not match real ones, tool compositions are not grounded in execution, and tasks rarely span more than one environment.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #databases #combinatorics

entry.title: Factorized MLLM Embeddings for Composed Image Retrieval. Composed Image Retrieval (CIR) aims to retrieve a target image given a reference image and a modification text.
entry.summary:
Composed Image Retrieval (CIR) aims to retrieve a target image given a reference image and a modification text. Although recent approaches leveraging Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have shown significant progress, we argue that the MLLM's compositional understanding remains underutilized. This stems from directly mapping composed queries into a retrieval embedding via contrastive supervision alone, without explicitly resolving the intended visual modifications.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #infosec #rag

entry.title: EvoTeam: Multi-Agent Collaboration via Evolving Teams. LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) rely on collaboration among specialized agents to solve complex tasks.
entry.summary:
LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) rely on collaboration among specialized agents to solve complex tasks. Existing methods improve MAS by refining the prompts, skills, and execution strategies of individual agents based on task feedback. However, improving individual agents does not necessarily lead to better team collaboration.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #agents
